keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 split-level nature photo of a calm pond, showing the part above the water and the part below the water at the same time. The water surface is a straight horizontal line at about 60 percent of the frame height from the top, so the part above the water fills more than half of the frame. One straight green reed stem stands vertically in the center of the frame, from the pond bottom, up through the water surface, to the top of the frame. Below the surface: clear greenish water, soft light rays, a few out-of-focus water plants far behind, sandy mud at the very bottom. Above the surface: soft out-of-focus green reeds and bright sky. On the underwater part of the stem, a little below the water surface, there is one short neat vertical row of tiny pale yellow oval dragonfly eggs laid into the stem. The eggs are small but clearly visible. Nothing else is on the stem. Soft diffused daylight, sharp focus on the stem. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the pond, the water surface line, the reed stem, background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The eggs are now empty, pale, see-through shells in the same spot. One tiny young dragonfly nymph clings to the underwater stem right next to the empty eggs. It is light brown, with six thin legs and large eyes, about four times the length of one egg. Only one nymph.

Edit this image. Keep everything exactly the same, including the pond, the water surface line, the reed stem, the empty eggs, background, lighting and camera angle. One newly emerged emperor dragonfly clings to the stem just above the empty skin, head up. Its body is soft and pale green, and its wings are still short, crumpled and milky. Only one dragonfly.

Edit this image. Keep everything exactly the same, including the pond, the water surface line, the reed stem, the empty eggs, the empty nymph skin, background, lighting and camera angle.
